root_cause.text: The BPF destructor kfunc type enforcement in `btf_check_dtor_kfuncs()` was guarded by the obsolete `CONFIG_CFI_CLANG` Kconfig symbol, so after the option was renamed to `CONFIG_CFI` the CFI-based type check for `btf_dtor_kfunc_t` was compiled out and invalid destructor kfuncs could still trigger CFI failures.
root_cause.evidence: The patch changes `if (IS_ENABLED(CONFIG_CFI_CLANG))` to `if (IS_ENABLED(CONFIG_CFI))` in `kernel/bpf/btf.c`, and both the CVE and commit message explicitly state that the old name “results in the code getting compiled out,” meaning “the CFI failures for btf_dtor_kfunc_t would still trigger.”

intent_record.intent_summary: Use the generic CONFIG_CFI gate so destructor kfunc type validation runs whenever CFI is enabled.
intent_record.what: The conditional compilation feature check in btf_check_dtor_kfuncs() was changed from IS_ENABLED(CONFIG_CFI_CLANG) to IS_ENABLED(CONFIG_CFI) around the destructor kfunc type validation block.
intent_record.how: At runtime, the destructor kfunc signature validation now executes whenever generic CFI support is enabled instead of only when the Clang-specific CFI config is enabled, ensuring the check applies under the current broader CFI configuration.

grouping_result.intent: Use the generic CONFIG_CFI gate so destructor kfunc type validation runs whenever CFI is enabled.

relevance_review.reason: The change directly replaces the obsolete CONFIG_CFI_CLANG guard with the generic CONFIG_CFI gate for destructor kfunc type validation, which is exactly the root cause described.

candidates.rationale: This obsolete Kconfig guard is the direct root cause: after the rename from CONFIG_CFI_CLANG to CONFIG_CFI, the destructor kfunc type validation block was compiled out even when CFI was enabled, allowing invalid destructor kfunc types to bypass enforcement and later trigger CFI failures.

vuln_statements.explanation: This obsolete Kconfig guard controlled whether the destructor kfunc type validation logic in btf_check_dtor_kfuncs() was compiled in. After the kernel option rename from CONFIG_CFI_CLANG to CONFIG_CFI, this condition evaluated false even when CFI was enabled, causing the CFI-based enforcement for btf_dtor_kfunc_t to be omitted and allowing invalid destructor kfuncs to bypass checking.

bic_trace_step.code_snippet:
commit 99fde4d0626176d03cea35c64a063df73816e64d
Author: Sami Tolvanen <samitolvanen@google.com>
Date:   Sat Jan 10 08:25:53 2026 +0000

    bpf, btf: Enforce destructor kfunc type with CFI
    
    Ensure that registered destructor kfuncs have the same type
    as btf_dtor_kfunc_t to avoid a kernel panic on systems with
    CONFIG_CFI enabled.
    
    Signed-off-by: Sami Tolvanen <samitolvanen@google.com>
    Acked-by: Yonghong Song <yonghong.song@linux.dev>
    Link: https://lore.kernel.org/r/
bic_trace_step.reason: The diff shows the relevant logic inside `btf_check_dtor_kfuncs()`, so it is sufficient to assess the issue. The root cause is that destructor kfunc type enforcement is guarded by the obsolete Kconfig symbol `CONFIG_CFI_CLANG` instead of the renamed `CONFIG_CFI`. In this commit version, the check is present only under `if (IS_ENABLED(CONFIG_CFI_CLANG)) { ... }`. Specifically, the code adds: `if (IS_ENABLED(CONFIG_CFI_CLANG)) { t = btf_type_by_id(btf, t->type); if (!btf_type_is_void(t)) return -EINVAL; }`. Because the enforcement is conditioned on `CONFIG_CFI_CLANG`, systems using the renamed `CONFIG_CFI` can still compile out this validation, which matches the described vulnerability. Therefore the vulnerable construct is present (`has_bug=true`), and the correct fix is not yet present (`is_fixed=false`) because the guard has not been updated to the proper `CONFIG_CFI` handling.

bic_trace_step.reason: The provided snippet is sufficient because it includes the full introduction of `btf_check_dtor_kfuncs()` and the call site in `register_btf_id_dtor_kfuncs()`. The root-cause vulnerability is specifically about the destructor kfunc type enforcement being conditionally compiled under the obsolete `CONFIG_CFI_CLANG` symbol, which would cause the check to be compiled out after the rename to `CONFIG_CFI`. In this commit, `btf_check_dtor_kfuncs()` is present and performs prototype validation unconditionally within the shown function body: it verifies the BTF ID is a function (`if (!dtor_func || !btf_type_is_func(dtor_func)) return -EINVAL;`), the prototype is a function prototype (`if (!dtor_func_proto || !btf_type_is_func_proto(dtor_func_proto)) return -EINVAL;`), the return type is void (`if (!t || !btf_type_is_void(t)) return -EINVAL;`), there is exactly one argument (`if (nr_args != 1) return -EINVAL;`), and that argument is a pointer (`if (!t || !btf_type_is_ptr(t)) return -EINVAL;`). The registration path also invokes this check directly: `ret = btf_check_dtor_kfuncs(btf, dtors, add_cnt); if (ret < 0) goto end;`. However, the specific fix for the reported vulnerability would be a correct CFI-gated type enforcement using `CONFIG_CFI` instead of `CONFIG_CFI_CLANG`. No such preprocessor guard or CFI-specific enforcement appears in this snippet at all, so the vulnerable construct described in the root cause is not present in the shown code, and the later fix is also not shown here.
